# Original Paper 00 — Complete Text Transcription
URL: https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/00-beyond-the-constraints-of-software/text/
Status: source-transcription
Conceptual source: Valto Loikkanen

 CONCEPTUAL WHITE PAPER / 00 / NOVEMBER 2026




 Beyond the Constraints
 of Software
 The transition toward an information-centric,
 intelligence-native world

 Conceptual source: Valto Loikkanen
 26 November 2026 | Version 1.0 | Conceptual synthesis



 Abstract
 The digital world has been organized around the limitations of software. Information is reduced to
 predefined storage structures, expressed through fixed presentation formats and made accessible
 through predetermined interfaces. Human activities and economic relationships have in turn
 adapted to what software can support. Artificial intelligence introduces the possibility of reversing
 these dependencies: information can be preserved in its original richness, interpreted when needed
 and served through interfaces and implementations that adapt to actual usage.

 This paper presents an umbrella thesis connecting Liquid Software, adaptive interfaces, capture for
 unknown future value, adaptive retrieval, individual and entity information systems, and degrees of
 decision freedom. Intelligence provides a general capability to respond to needs; software becomes
 an increasingly fluid optimization. Relatively durable information, shared semantics, capability
 requirements and human-defined boundaries maintain coherence and continuity.


    Information provides continuity. Human decisions define the
    boundaries. Intelligence fulfills needs, with software emerging as an
    optimization.

 This paper is a synthesis of concepts articulated by Valto Loikkanen in the source discussion. It is a proposed paradigm
 and reference map, not a claim that the technologies are fully realized or that every underlying idea is new.




BEYOND THE CONSTRAINTS OF SOFTWARE / CONCEPTUAL SOURCE: VALTO LOIKKANEN                                                     01
 WHITE PAPER 00 / 01



 The historical bottleneck
 Software made the digital economy possible, but the effort required to build, distribute and
 maintain it also made it a structural constraint. To make computation reliable and affordable,
 developers specified in advance what information would be captured, which operations would be
 available and how users would interact with them. Scale rewarded standardization, and users and
 organizations adapted to the resulting applications.

 This is more than a development productivity problem. The limitations of software influence what
 can be recorded, which relationships can be expressed, what services are economically viable and
 how work is organized. A system designed for anticipated needs often becomes an obstacle to
 needs that emerge later.

 Four inversions
  Domain               Historical constraint                          Intelligence-native direction

  Storage              Anticipated queries define what is             Preserve authorized source richness
                       retained.                                      before choosing retrieval structures.

  Retrieval            Prebuilt queries and indexes define what       Interpret new needs; optimize recurring
                       can be found efficiently.                      retrieval patterns.

  Interface            Information is fitted into a fixed artifact,   Derive the representation and interaction
                       UI or endpoint.                                from context and intent.

  Software             Available functionality determines what        Let actual needs determine which
                       can be done.                                   implementations are useful.



 Intelligence first, software second
 The proposed reversal is to establish general intelligent capability before deciding where dedicated
 software is needed. An intelligent system can interpret a new request and attempt to fulfill it
 directly. Repetition and operational requirements then justify deterministic code, caching, indexes
 or other optimizations. This does not eliminate software: it changes why software exists, when it is
 produced and how long it remains useful.

 The thesis is a direction of travel, not a prediction that every domain will become fluid.
 Safety-critical controls, contractual guarantees, real-time systems and other deterministic
 requirements can justify stable implementations from the outset. The point is to avoid unnecessary
 rigidity, not to maximize change.


    We have organized the world around what software could do.
    Increasingly, we can organize software around what the world
    actually needs.




BEYOND THE CONSTRAINTS OF SOFTWARE / CONCEPTUAL SOURCE: VALTO LOIKKANEN                                           02
 WHITE PAPER 00 / 02



 Information before structure
 Storage is the deepest of the historical constraints because it determines which evidence survives.
 A report, interface or application can be regenerated; discarded observations may be impossible to
 reconstruct. When a conversation is reduced to the fields of a CRM system, information that was
 not anticipated by the schema is often lost.

 A capture-first architecture preserves authorized original information in the richest practical form:
 text, documents, images, audio, video, spatial recordings and sensor observations. A hypothetical
 near-maximal capture of an experience might include synchronized 3D video, spatial audio, thermal
 imagery, LiDAR and environmental measurements. No set of sensors records all reality, but richer
 capture expands the questions that can be asked later.

 The birds behind the observer
 Suppose a person walks through a park without noticing birds behind them. Years later they ask
 what the birds were doing and whether they appeared healthy. Spatial and multimodal recordings
 could permit retrospective analysis of behavior and visible health indicators. A predefined table
 containing only location and walking duration could not answer those questions. Even rich evidence
 may not establish actual health; the system must distinguish observations, interpretations and
 unknowns.

   Source evidence                   Preserve original recordings, timestamps, provenance and relevant context.

   Interpretation                    Extract observations, relationships, propositions and uncertainty as needs
                                     emerge.

   Derived structures                Generate SQL tables, spatial indexes, graphs, vector indexes or other
                                     retrieval representations.

   Reprocessing                      Revisit the original evidence with improved models or newly relevant
                                     questions.


 SQL is valuable as an efficient retrieval and transactional technology, not inherently inferior as a
 storage technology. The architectural error is allowing a narrowly anticipated retrieval schema to
 determine the full extent of what is preserved. Authoritative structured facts may themselves be
 canonical when they originate as structured records. Derived representations should not silently
 replace richer original evidence.


    Capture without needing to know what will be asked. Structure
    according to what is asked. Optimize according to how often it is
    asked.

 Privacy, consent, data minimization, retention, cost and legal obligations govern capture. Maximum future value means
 maximum appropriate richness within those boundaries, not indiscriminate surveillance.




BEYOND THE CONSTRAINTS OF SOFTWARE / CONCEPTUAL SOURCE: VALTO LOIKKANEN                                                  03
 WHITE PAPER 00 / 03



 The interface becomes adaptive
 Documents, slide decks, infographics, dashboards and applications can be understood as different
 interfaces to information. Historically each has required separate production, formatting and
 maintenance. Software also limits information through fixed screens, forms and workflows. In both
 cases the presentation format precedes the information need and constrains its expression.

 UI on the fly reverses this relationship. Information exists independently of a presentation, and an
 interface is generated or selected according to the actual recipient and situation. It may be a
 temporary view, a reusable artifact, an interactive tool or a conversation. A snapshot can still be
 retained when it is itself evidence, a publication or a formal record.

  Dimension               Determines the interaction

  What                    The information or capability needed, its nature and relevant relationships.

  To whom                 Recipient, role, expertise, language, accessibility and authority.

  Where                   Device, physical or operational environment, available attention and context.

  Why                     The purpose: understanding, communicating, deciding, retrieving or acting.

  How                     The resulting presentation, request and response format, derived from the above
                          or explicitly requested.



 A unified human and machine interface
 Humans may express intent in speech, text or actions; agents and applications may use structured
 requests or natural language. The same semantics, permissions and capability contracts can
 underpin both. A machine requester can specify the desired information and output shape using
 GraphQL, REST-style requests or other agreed conventions; a human can describe an equivalent
 need in words.

 The choice of request format should not prescribe the responding implementation. A
 GraphQL-shaped request can be fulfilled agentically, deterministically or through a hybrid path.
 Standard GraphQL still requires a valid schema, and REST does not by itself define a response
 schema. A practical system therefore needs supported request grammars, discoverable or
 negotiated contracts and validation rules. Dynamic semantics must not silently break a declared
 contract.


    What, to whom, where and why determine how. The interface is an
    outcome, not a starting point.




BEYOND THE CONSTRAINTS OF SOFTWARE / CONCEPTUAL SOURCE: VALTO LOIKKANEN                                     04
 WHITE PAPER 00 / 04



 Liquid Software
 Liquid Software is a proposed paradigm in which software implementations can continuously
 emerge, adapt, solidify and retire according to actual needs, within governed semantic and technical
 boundaries. It brings together the earlier ideas of UI on the fly and backend on the fly, and extends
 the same logic to machine interfaces, integrations, retrieval and execution.

 The central change is not merely the generation of code. The underlying capability may already be
 available through intelligence. Dedicated software becomes useful when it improves speed, cost,
 predictability, repeatability or other operational characteristics. The capability and its contract
 remain relatively independent of the particular implementation.

 A reversible lifecycle
   1. Emergence                A novel or infrequent need is interpreted and fulfilled through intelligence
                               where possible.

   2. Observation              Recurring semantic patterns, costs, latencies, reliability and dependencies are
                               measured.

   3. Solidification           Validated code, indexes, caches, skills or services take over appropriate parts
                               of fulfillment.

   4. Adaptation               Implementations are regenerated, combined or revised as information, needs
                               and requirements evolve.

   5. Retirement               Unused optimizations are removed or archived; valid contracts retain an
                               appropriate fallback.


 This is not a one-way journey from agentic to deterministic. Demand can be seasonal or short-lived.
 A temporary project may create intense demand for a particular view or API, followed by little use.
 If the need returns, the implementation can be reactivated or regenerated. Some needs will always
 be best served through a hybrid of intelligence and stable software.

 Stable foundations make fluidity possible
 Canonical documentation, terminology, capability requirements documents (CRDs), reusable skills,
 design conventions, permissions, business rules and technical standards define what must remain
 coherent. They also guide agents on where to look and how to reason when a particular
 requirement is not predefined. Custom behavior is thereby constrained by shared principles rather
 than left arbitrary.


    Liquid Software is governed fluidity, not software without structure.




BEYOND THE CONSTRAINTS OF SOFTWARE / CONCEPTUAL SOURCE: VALTO LOIKKANEN                                          05
 WHITE PAPER 00 / 05



 The self-optimizing information system
 A concrete technical realization is an adaptive retrieval and fulfillment layer that can accept
 requests in supported formats without requiring every possible semantic query to be implemented
 in advance. Shared documentation and terminology make the request interpretable. The receiving
 system selects a fulfillment path independently of whether the requester is a human, agent or
 traditional application.

   Request                      Identify the requester, represented principal, purpose and expected response
                                contract.

   Interpret and authorize      Resolve semantics and scope; check permissions and relevant obligations.

   Fulfill                      Route to agentic hybrid retrieval, deterministic software or a combination.

   Validate and respond         Check schema, provenance, freshness, constraints and uncertainty; deliver
                                the agreed representation.

   Observe and improve          Monitor semantic request patterns and operational outcomes; identify
                                candidates for optimization.



 The nightly optimization process
 A monitoring agent can observe daily and weekly usage, group equivalent requests and evaluate
 the cost and benefit of producing more permanent retrieval structures or API implementations. A
 scheduled optimization run can propose creation, updates, consolidation or retirement. Frequency
 is a strong signal; latency targets, correctness, sensitivity, implementation cost and service
 commitments also determine whether an optimization is justified.

 The optimizer must not bypass the authority and semantic checks that apply to agentic retrieval. It
 should test against CRDs and representative queries, verify access controls and freshness, measure
 regressions, deploy under defined approval rules and preserve rollback. Retiring a particular
 implementation must not remove an externally committed capability unless that contract is
 changed appropriately.

 Illustrative example
 An entity frequently asks for a weekly view of open commitments by owner. Initially the system
 interprets its documentation and retrieves evidence across sources. Repetition warrants a derived
 index and validated query implementation. Later, the activity ends and the index is retired if no
 obligations require it. A future valid request can fall back to intelligent retrieval without changing
 the meaning of the requested information.


    The request defines the need and the expected response. Actual
    usage determines the implementation.




BEYOND THE CONSTRAINTS OF SOFTWARE / CONCEPTUAL SOURCE: VALTO LOIKKANEN                                        06
 WHITE PAPER 00 / 06



 Individuals and entities as anchors
 At the architectural level, the model distinguishes two types of information principal: an individual
 and an entity. PIOS represents the personal information, intelligence and continuity of an individual;
 EIOS represents the corresponding needs of an entity. These are conceptual anchors, not a
 requirement that every technical resource have a single physical endpoint or that legal ownership
 of all information be exclusive.

 The implementation-level requester can still be a human, an agent or an application. It may act
 directly or indirectly on behalf of an individual or entity. An agent can initiate a request to serve a
 delegated objective without a human explicitly formulating that particular request.

  Independent dimension                   Possibilities

  Principal                               Individual (PIOS) or entity (EIOS)

  Operational actor                       Human, agent or application

  Interaction                             Natural language, structured request, protocol or other agreed format

  Fulfillment                             Agentic, deterministic or hybrid


 The immediate requester, represented principal, ultimate beneficiary and purpose should be
 distinguished for authority and accountability. Neither the actor nor its interaction format
 determines the other side's implementation. PIOS and EIOS can exchange information with each
 other through established sharing arrangements, retaining separate control and continuity.

 Complementary architectural concepts
  Concept                                Role in the architecture

  PIOS / EIOS                            Persistent identity, canonical information, knowledge, objectives and
                                         continuity.

  PAIX                                   Framework for establishing contact and coordinating interactions
                                         between parties.

  CRDs                                   Implementation-independent capability requirements and acceptance
                                         boundaries.

  Personal Application Ecosystem         Applications as replaceable mechanisms serving the individual and
                                         their information.

  Documentation and semantics            Shared vocabulary, provenance, governing rules and guidance for
                                         resolving unspecified needs.

 These concepts are complementary rather than mandatory dependencies. A system may adopt adaptive interfaces or
 capture-first storage independently of PIOS, EIOS or PAIX.




BEYOND THE CONSTRAINTS OF SOFTWARE / CONCEPTUAL SOURCE: VALTO LOIKKANEN                                           07
 WHITE PAPER 00 / 07



 Degrees of decision freedom
 As the rigidity of software decreases, human decision speed may become a major constraint, insofar
 as humans retain ultimate authority. The answer is not to eliminate human control, but to increase
 the leverage of decisions already made. Human sovereignty does not require separate human
 approval of every operational step.

 Decisions are never made in a vacuum. Every decision is made within an existing space of freedom,
 shaped by applicable law, rights, agreements, values, resources, circumstances and prior decisions.
 Higher-level decisions can establish a lower-level decision space without prescribing each decision
 made within it.

   External boundaries         Applicable law, rights, contractual commitments, physical conditions and
                               available resources.

   Principal decisions         Purpose, values, strategic objectives and decisions reserved to the individual
                               or authorized entity governance.

   Delegated freedom           Objectives, responsibilities, budgets, permissions, methods and scope of
                               independent action.

   Operational choices         Contextual decisions and execution within inherited boundaries.

   Escalation                  Conflicting objectives, insufficient authority, exceeded limits or reserved
                               decisions return to the appropriate authority.


 Autonomy is multidimensional: an agent may have wide freedom to select a retrieval method,
 narrow freedom to commit money and no freedom to disclose private information. The same is true
 of humans working within organizations. Guidance can be distinguished from strict prohibitions;
 uncertainties and conflicts must be resolved rather than assumed away.

 Documentation, CRDs, permissions and policies are therefore more than development instructions.
 They can represent accumulated human decisions, made durable and applicable to future actions.
 Systems need traceability, revocable delegation, clear escalation, appropriate oversight and
 mechanisms to update those decisions as circumstances change.


    Higher-level decisions define the space of freedom for lower-level
    decisions, rather than requiring every lower-level decision to be
    repeated.




BEYOND THE CONSTRAINTS OF SOFTWARE / CONCEPTUAL SOURCE: VALTO LOIKKANEN                                         08
 WHITE PAPER 00 / 08



 The internet beyond applications
 The Internet on One Page model, provided by Loikkanen, describes the digital economy through
 fundamental activities, information flows, information types and revenue models. Its logic does not
 depend on particular applications. Liquid Software provides a possible technical means of serving
 these activities without fixing them to a permanent application or platform.




 Figure 1. The Internet on One Page. Source: Valto Loikkanen, diagram supplied in the source discussion. Cropped to the
 diagram boundary.

 Create, Control, Promote, Connect, Discover, Acquire and Consume remain meaningful regardless
 of who performs them or what software is used. They can be supported by agents, applications or
 people acting for individuals and entities. Information can carry promotional, public-domain, owned
 or private/personal value; the relevant rights and access conditions govern exchange.

 Licensing, advertising, transaction fees, commerce and subscriptions are likewise durable economic
 arrangements. An agent could discover licensable information, evaluate terms, obtain authorized
 access and utilize it for its principal without a dedicated marketplace UI. Intermediaries and
 platforms may still deliver trust, liquidity and coordination; their role need not be dictated solely by
 software constraints.

 The opportunity is to separate the enduring economic activity from its transient technological
 implementation. Trust, authority, information quality and human governance become increasingly
 important as software becomes easier to adapt.




BEYOND THE CONSTRAINTS OF SOFTWARE / CONCEPTUAL SOURCE: VALTO LOIKKANEN                                                   09
 WHITE PAPER 00 / 09



 From thesis to practice
 The proposed concepts share a reversal: preserve what has enduring value, make boundaries
 explicit and allow implementations and representations to evolve around actual needs. They
 operate at different levels and should remain independently understandable and adoptable. The
 reference architecture is a way of combining them, not the only way to implement them.

 A practical transition pathway
   Establish foundations        Identify canonical sources, ownership, permissions, terminology, CRDs and
                                guidance for unspecified cases.

   Introduce adaptive access    Support context-driven human and machine requests; separate response
                                contracts from fulfillment.

   Preserve richer evidence     Retain appropriate source information with provenance; distinguish canonical
                                and derived representations.

   Observe actual demand        Instrument usage with privacy-preserving monitoring and identify repetitive
                                needs.

   Optimize under               Create and retire validated software and retrieval structures; benchmark
   governance                   against agentic and hybrid paths.

   Increase decision leverage   Define delegated freedom, escalation and reserved decisions; adjust
                                authority through deliberate review.



 Open research and validation questions
 How can agents converge on consistent semantics without rigidly predetermining every request?
 How should evolving contracts be discovered, negotiated and versioned? How can equivalence
 between agentic and deterministic responses be tested, including uncertainty and provenance?
 What retention choices best balance future information value, rights, environmental cost and
 storage economics? When does the cost of autonomous optimization outweigh its benefit? How
 can decision boundaries be made inspectable and enforceable across independently operated
 systems?

 These questions define a research and implementation agenda. The architecture should be tested
 through concrete workloads, measuring accuracy, permission compliance, latency, cost, portability
 and the ability to retire implementations without loss of continuity.


    Define what must remain consistent. Allow everything else to adapt
    intelligently.




BEYOND THE CONSTRAINTS OF SOFTWARE / CONCEPTUAL SOURCE: VALTO LOIKKANEN                                        10
 WHITE PAPER 00 / 10



 A complementary body of work
 This umbrella paper provides the shared thesis and entry point for a proposed collection of
 independent white papers. The following roadmap separates foundational thinking, paradigms,
 technical realization and wider implications. Titles are working titles; the remaining papers are
 proposed, not represented here as completed publications.

  No.      Proposed independent white paper                          Distinct focus

  01       The Software Bottleneck                                   Historical rigidity and its consequences.

  02       Intelligence First, Software Second                       Intelligence as capability; software as
                                                                     optimization.

  03       Degrees of Decision Freedom                               Delegation, boundaries and human
                                                                     sovereignty.

  04       Liquid Software                                           Governed, reversible software evolution.

  05       The Adaptive Interface                                    Unified contextual human and machine
                                                                     interaction.

  06       Capture for Unknown Future Value                          Preserve authorized source richness.

  07       Adaptive Information Retrieval                            Derived and evolving retrieval structures.

  08       The Self-Optimizing Information System                    Usage-driven monitoring and optimization.

  09       Beyond Predefined APIs                                    Request contracts independent of
                                                                     implementation.

  10       Documentation as Executable Foundations                   Semantics, CRDs and persistent guidance.

  12       The Lifecycle of Liquid Software                          Transitions among fulfillment modes.

  13       The Internet Beyond Applications                          Economic activities and information flows.

  14       From Software-Centric to Information-Centric              Reversal of constraints across the layers.
           Computing

 The intent is independent value, mutual complementarity and collective coherence. Each paper should define its own
 contribution without requiring adoption of the entire collection.




BEYOND THE CONSTRAINTS OF SOFTWARE / CONCEPTUAL SOURCE: VALTO LOIKKANEN                                               11
 WHITE PAPER 00 / 11



 Conclusion and source note
 The enduring elements of the digital world are not necessarily the applications through which we
 currently experience it. They are the individuals and entities being served, the information and
 knowledge they retain, the intentions and relationships they establish, the economic activities they
 undertake and the decisions that govern their conduct.

 When intelligence makes information accessible without extensive prior specification, storage can
 preserve future value, interfaces can serve immediate context and software can evolve in response
 to actual demand. The resulting world need not be less coherent or less human-controlled.
 Coherence comes from shared semantics, documentation, capabilities and enforceable boundaries;
 sovereignty comes from authority and degrees of decision freedom.

 This is a proposed change in the relationship between information, intelligence and software. Its
 realization depends on reliable implementations, evidence-preserving practices, interoperability,
 sound governance and the deliberate protection of rights.


 Information provides continuity.
 Human decisions define the boundaries.
 Intelligence fulfills needs.
 Software adapts.

 Conceptual source and scope
 Valto Loikkanen, source discussion on Liquid Software, UI on the fly, backend on the fly, unified
 interfaces, PIOS, EIOS, PAIX, CRDs, information capture, information retrieval and degrees of
 decision freedom, 25-26 November 2026. The Internet on One Page diagram was supplied by
 Loikkanen in the discussion.

 The paper was synthesized and edited with AI assistance from that discussion. The source
 attribution identifies Loikkanen as the source of the conceptual framing and synthesis presented
 here. It does not assert exclusive authorship or priority over established technical concepts or
 terminology. No independent literature review or empirical validation was conducted for this
 version.

 Suggested citation
 Loikkanen, Valto (conceptual source). (2026). Beyond the Constraints of Software: The Transition
 Toward an Information-Centric, Intelligence-Native World. Conceptual White Paper 00, version 1.0,
 26 November 2026.

# Liquid Software: The Economics of Execution
URL: https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/economics-of-execution/
Status: published
Conceptual source: Valto Loikkanen

# Liquid Software: The Economics of Execution

*A dynamic framework for when intelligence should act directly, when software should materialize, and when existing implementations should evolve or dissolve.*

Conceptual source: **Valto Loikkanen**. Supplied conceptual whitepaper, **version 2.0, 27 November 2026**, nine pages. This is a distinct expanded economics paper alongside the umbrella paper and sixteen companion research drafts. Its printed edition date is established; its earlier conceptual origin date is not.

## The economic question

Which feasible way of fulfilling a need delivers the greatest cumulative net value over the relevant time horizon?

The paper compares direct intelligent execution, reusable skills, deterministic functions, software modules, dedicated applications and combinations of these. It treats that choice as reversible. A deterministic implementation can be the right initial choice, remain useful for years, or later give way to another realization.

The objective includes time to value, full lifecycle expenditure, transition and restoration costs, failure risk, foregone opportunities and the value of retaining flexibility. Lower coding cost and lower inference cost each change the comparison; neither alone establishes the winner.

## What the expanded edition covers

| <span style="white-space:nowrap">Pages</span> | Contribution |
| --- | --- |
| 1–2 | Entity-level economics; intelligence using available tools; a reversible continuum of realizations; the constraints introduced by premature determinism. |
| 3–4 | Comparable outcomes and authority boundaries; the full lifecycle of both agentic and software paths; net value, investment risk and double transition cost. |
| 5 | Value delivered during learning and parallel development; changing inference and software-production economics; a limited break-even model. |
| 6 | Optimization at capability, contract and component level; modular models, processing and infrastructure; durable context outside replaceable runtimes. |
| 7 | Source preservation separated from processing investment; selective caching and preprocessing around demand, freshness and purpose. |
| 8–9 | An operating loop for informed selection; maturity bias; explicit scope limits and eight references. |

The vehicle and humanoid comparison is a conceptual analogy, explicitly qualified in the PDF. The diagrams illustrate possible sequences and combinations; they are not deployment evidence or mandatory maturity stages.

## Read the complete source

The [original PDF](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/economics-of-execution/v2.0.pdf) preserves every supplied byte and all four diagrams. The [complete text transcription](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/economics-of-execution/text/) preserves the extracted wording of all nine pages, including the source note. PDF extraction preserves text rather than visual geometry; consult the PDF for diagrams and layout.

The printed source credits Loikkanen as conceptual source. It does not identify a model or state an AI-writing attribution. This overview, the associated concept page and the reference audit are AI-assisted editorial work prepared from that source. The earlier economics edition and the *AI Maturity, Maturity Bias and Informed Selection* companion mentioned on page 8 were not supplied; no comparison with their full contents is claimed.

## A decision framework, with evidence limits

The paper is a conceptual framework, not a measured demonstration that agents, local hardware or one vendor architecture always cost less. Its source note makes this limitation explicit.

Pendo's 2019 report describes feature usage in its own sampled products and an extrapolated R&D estimate. GAO's July 2026 Technology Modernization Fund review distinguishes cash-savings expectations from other benefits and examines a particular public-sector portfolio. The UK supply-chain study reports qualitative accounts of system adoption and a few reversals. These findings have different denominators and measures and must remain separate.

Stanford's historical inference-price comparison concerns approximate GPT-3.5-level MMLU performance, from November 2022 to October 2024. It does not measure total agent costs, owned-hardware economics or future prices. CRD provides a way to describe capabilities separately from realizations. MDIL/Kide's public claims illustrate a proposed modular architecture; they are not independently verified comparative benchmarks.

The cited GAO-11-53 page and Washington Post payroll article could not be read during this intake. The original claims remain attributable to the supplied PDF. An official Senate report independently corroborates ECSS cancellation after more than $1 billion was spent, but does not verify every detail of the inaccessible GAO status update. The D.C. payroll amount and cost composition remain unverified in this review.

## Follow the argument

[Capability Economics](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/capability-economics/) develops an independent explanation, a hypothetical time-to-value example, the decision model and proposed tests. Related concepts are [Intelligence First](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/intelligence-first/), [Liquid Software](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/liquid-software/), [Self-Optimization](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/self-optimizing-system/) and [Adaptive Information Retrieval](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/adaptive-information-retrieval/).

## Reference audit

The full bibliography remains in the PDF and transcription. These links identify the originals and the scope of this review.

1. [Pendo, The 2019 Feature Adoption Report](https://www.pendo.io/resources/the-2019-feature-adoption-report/): main report and methodology read; vendor cohort, reported extrapolation, not a universal waste rate.
2. [GAO-26-107737, Technology Modernization Fund](https://files.gao.gov/reports/GAO-26-107737/index.html): highlights, completed-project findings and relevant methodology read; not the whole report.
3. [GAO-11-53](https://www.gao.gov/products/gao-11-53): inaccessible during intake; later recommendation-status wording not verified. Supplement: [U.S. Senate Report 114-162](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CRPT-114srpt162/html/CRPT-114srpt162.htm), relevant ECSS passage read.
4. [UK government, use of IT systems for managing supply chains](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/use-of-it-systems-by-uk-businesses-for-managing-supply-chain-data/use-of-it-systems-by-uk-businesses-for-managing-supply-chains): methodology and relevant adoption, removal and cost sections read; qualitative evidence.

# Economics of Execution v2 — Complete Text Transcription
URL: https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/economics-of-execution/text/
Status: source-transcription
Conceptual source: Valto Loikkanen

          LIQUID SOFTWARE / WHITEPAPER                                        EXPANDED EDITION | NOV 2026




01 / THESIS



Liquid Software:
The Economics of Execution
A dynamic framework for when intelligence should act directly, when software should
materialize, and when existing implementations should evolve or dissolve.

Conceptual source: Valto Loikkanen | Version 2.0 | November 27, 2026


Abstract
AI changes not only the cost of producing software, but also the need to produce it. Work can be
performed directly by agents, through reusable skills and specialized components, through
deterministic software, or through a combination of these. Liquid Software makes the choice between
these realizations a continuous economic and architectural decision.

The objective is to maximize risk-adjusted cumulative net value over time, including time to value, total
lifecycle costs, foregone opportunities, the cost of failed adoption and transitions, and the flexibility
lost when behavior is fixed. Modularity extends this principle to models, capabilities, information
processing and infrastructure.


   Intelligence is the default capability. Software is an optimization.


From market-level to entity-level economics
SaaS has made even narrow applications viable by spreading design, development and maintenance
across many users and organizations. When an individual or organization can fulfill needs directly with
agents and create software on demand, a dedicated implementation must justify its value within that
entity. External SaaS, shared components and existing infrastructure remain legitimate alternatives.

Lower software development cost alone does not justify more software: the cost and capability of
direct agentic execution are changing at the same time. The question is what should exist, in what form,
at what granularity, and for how long.


   You don’t build a house for one night visit or road to walk by once.
   Valto Loikkanen, November 2026




Valto Loikkanen | Conceptual whitepaper | November 2026                                                   1
          LIQUID SOFTWARE / WHITEPAPER                                                       EXPANDED EDITION | NOV 2026




02 / OPERATING PARADIGM



Intelligence can use any tool
Consider a self-driving car and a sufficiently capable general-purpose humanoid. The self-driving car is
an advanced, intelligence-empowered vehicle. The humanoid could instead drive a decades-old car,
operate a truck, ride a bicycle, make food and perform digital chores concurrently where safe and
feasible. The intelligence is not permanently bound to a single tool. This is a conceptual analogy, not a
claim about today’s humanoid capabilities.

  Intelligence embedded in a tool                               Intelligence that can use tools

  Self-driving car                                              Humanoid driving a compatible existing vehicle

  Specialized industrial robot                                  General-purpose worker using specialized machinery

  AI-enabled application                                        Agent using existing software, APIs and tools

  Software-defined agent workflow                               Agent choosing and composing capabilities as needed


A high-utilization autonomous taxi fleet or a factory robot can still justify specialization. The difference
is that specialized infrastructure is chosen for demonstrated advantages rather than treated as the
prerequisite for intelligent work.

The execution continuum

    Direct agentic               Reusable             Deterministic               Software                Dedicated
      execution                    skills              functions                  modules                 software



Figure 1. Different steps of an activity may occupy different points. The continuum is reversible, not a mandatory maturity
progression.

Software is also a constraint
A road accelerates travel along a chosen route, but can become a barrier when it has too few exits.
Software encodes assumptions about workflows, data, interaction and rules; these may restrict both
humans and agents. Premature determinism fixes behavior before variability and exceptions are
understood. Expose functions independently, allow alternative paths, and retain agentic fallback where
permitted.


   Materialize determinism only where its benefits exceed its lifecycle
   costs and the value of the flexibility it removes.




Valto Loikkanen | Conceptual whitepaper | November 2026                                                                       2
           LIQUID SOFTWARE / WHITEPAPER                                                       EXPANDED EDITION | NOV 2026




03 / ECONOMIC DECISION MODEL



Beyond runtime cost
Compare all candidate realizations against the same required outcome, quality, latency, reliability,
safety and authority boundaries. Account for the full lifecycle, including the cost of enabling
intelligence itself. Do not equate lower inference cost or lower coding cost with superior economics.

  Lifecycle dimension         Agentic realization                              Software realization

  Design                      Purpose, constraints, context, acceptance        Requirements, architecture, interface
                              criteria                                         design

  Build & deploy              Skills, permissions, tools, runtime setup        Development, integration, testing, rollout

  Execution                   Inference, retries, tool use, time,              Compute, infrastructure, operating time
                              supervision

  Assurance                   Evaluation, uncertainty, verification,           Tests, monitoring, validation, controls
                              controls

  Maintenance                 Context, skills, models, runtime upkeep          Code, dependencies, security,
                                                                               integrations

  Adaptation                  Changes to goals, instructions or tools          Changes to code, data models and
                                                                               workflows

  Retirement                  Remove or replace realization; preserve          Decommission, migration, restoration
                              records


Optimize net value, not just cost
For each alternative and plausible demand scenario, estimate the discounted value delivered over the
relevant horizon, subtract full lifecycle expenditure, transition costs and losses attributable to rigidity or
failure. Compare against the best feasible alternative, including doing nothing. Account for foregone
business opportunities without counting the same loss twice.


   Decision objective: maximize expected cumulative net business value
   over time, subject to required quality, risk, performance and
   governance constraints.

A low-cost execution path can be economically inferior if it delays revenue or blocks a better outcome. A fixed
implementation can be justified before repeated use where safety, legal obligations, predictable latency or reliability require
it.




Valto Loikkanen | Conceptual whitepaper | November 2026                                                                      3
          LIQUID SOFTWARE / WHITEPAPER                                                   EXPANDED EDITION | NOV 2026




04 / EVIDENCE AND INVESTMENT RISK



The cost of software that fails to create
value
Unused, underused and unsuccessful implementations are different forms of economic exposure.
Evidence from both public audits and product analytics demonstrates the problem, although there is no
reliable universal failure rate for all software.

  Evidence                                   What it establishes

  80% of features rarely or never used       Pendo’s 2019 product usage study reported this share for the average
                                             product in its data. It estimated up to $29.5B in cloud software R&D
                                             associated with these features. [1]

  4 of 6 completed projects missed or        GAO’s July 2026 review of eligible US Technology Modernization Fund
  were off track for savings                 projects, measured as of June 2025. Seven of the 68 reviewed projects
                                             had been cancelled and no longer expected savings. [2]

  $1B already spent before cancellation      GAO reported that the US Air Force cancelled ECSS after around $1B
                                             had been expended, with another $1B expected and limited projected
                                             capability. [3]

  $34M+ to change and change back            The Washington Post reported this cost for Washington, D.C.’s
                                             migration to and return from a replacement payroll system. [5]


These are different populations and measures, not comparable failure rates. Pendo is vendor research; GAO provides
official public-sector audit findings. The D.C. figure is a reported historical case, not an audit estimate.

Double transition cost
Introducing an unsuccessful human-facing system can cause disruption twice: first through training,
migration and process redesign; then through retraining, data reconciliation and restoration. UK
government research in 2023 reported a few such reversals when replacement supply-chain systems
proved worse, unusable or otherwise unsuitable. [4]

The damage can extend beyond expenditure to customer loss, employee frustration, deferred
initiatives and diminished confidence. These consequences are distinct from the original build cost and
should be included when comparing alternatives.


   The greatest economic benefit may be the software that never needs
   to be created.




Valto Loikkanen | Conceptual whitepaper | November 2026                                                              4
          LIQUID SOFTWARE / WHITEPAPER                                                       EXPANDED EDITION | NOV 2026




05 / TIME AND CHANGING ECONOMICS



Value before infrastructure
Direct agentic execution, where feasible, lets a need be fulfilled before a dedicated implementation
exists. Actual execution then exposes frequency, exceptions, cost, requirements and reuse
opportunities. The organization can invest in software after evidence emerges rather than wait for a
speculative build.

Conventional software-first sequence

         Design                           Build                       Deploy                          Value

Agent-first sequence, where feasible

                                            Business value through execution


                        Function A                         Module B                         Function C

Figure 2. Illustrative time-to-value comparison; software development can occur alongside ongoing work. Agentic
execution also has setup time, and some tasks require upfront software.

Opportunity cost includes the value of delayed outcomes, lost customers or market windows, and
scarce management, employee or capital resources diverted from other work. Deferring a permanent
investment also preserves the option to change direction as evidence improves. Even identical eventual
software can produce very different cumulative business value.

The economic threshold moves
Stanford’s 2025 AI Index reports that the inference price for a model at approximately GPT-3.5-level
MMLU performance fell from $20 to $0.07 per million tokens between November 2022 and October
2024, over 280-fold. [6] This is a benchmark-specific historical comparison, not a measure of
whole-agent costs or a guarantee of future declines.

Local models and owned hardware may lower marginal cost compared with retail API pricing,
particularly at high utilization. Compare full hardware amortization, electricity, operations, model
quality, latency, retries and supervision. Software production costs are also falling, so reassess both
sides, not only inference.

A simple break-even model: if fixed incremental software cost is F, agentic cost per successful execution is a and software
cost is s, the threshold is F/(a−s) when a exceeds s. Actual decisions also require time, maintenance, quality, demand
uncertainty, flexibility and opportunity cost.




Valto Loikkanen | Conceptual whitepaper | November 2026                                                                       5
          LIQUID SOFTWARE / WHITEPAPER                                                         EXPANDED EDITION | NOV 2026




06 / MODULARITY



Optimize every capability, not every
application
Modularity is the central architectural enabler. Optimize at the smallest economically meaningful unit,
not at the level of an entire application or agent. A component should be independently reusable and
replaceable while retaining a coherent purpose, interaction contract and assurance requirements.

The CRD as the stable semantic layer
Valto Loikkanen’s Capability Requirements Document (CRD) framework distinguishes a Capability MLE
(Minimum Logical Element), its Interaction Contract MLEs, and one or more realizations. A CRD
specifies a complete contextually meaningful ability independently of the current implementation. [7]
Individual contracts or internal operations can be assigned different realization mechanisms.

Capability MLE / CRD
Purpose, requirements, boundaries, interaction contracts, evidence and unknowns


      Advanced                  Small local             Deterministic               Software                 Existing
   reasoning model               model                 reasoning layer              function               service / API



Figure 3. Illustrative realization options. They are composable alternatives, not a ranking or a fixed sequence.

Use the least costly realization that demonstrably meets the capability’s requirements. An advanced
model may interpret novel cases; a smaller local model may classify; a deterministic rule may validate;
existing APIs may execute authorized actions. Route uncertain cases to higher-capability models or
humans as appropriate.

MDIL/Kide illustrates another emerging option: the provider describes declared deterministic reasoning
separated from language generation, with traceable decisions. [8] Such components may reduce
repeated probabilistic reasoning for suitable tasks. Their actual economics, suitability and availability
must be evaluated rather than assumed.

Modularity across the stack
Compose agents, skills, models, contracts, functions, data processing and infrastructure independently.
Preserve durable context and records outside replaceable runtimes. Agents may be instantiated for a
task and dismissed without losing organizational knowledge. More modularity increases reuse and
off-ramps, but coordination, testing and interface costs still matter.




Valto Loikkanen | Conceptual whitepaper | November 2026                                                                    6
          LIQUID SOFTWARE / WHITEPAPER                                                        EXPANDED EDITION | NOV 2026




07 / INFORMATION ECONOMICS



Process information for a purpose
The same reasoning applies to information. Data availability is not in itself sufficient justification for
processing it. Extraction, classification, embedding, summarization and relationship construction
consume resources, can become stale, and may never contribute to a retrieved answer or action.


   Decide what processing is needed for a purpose. Defer additional
   processing unless retrieval or an established requirement justifies it.


    Retain source              Process on             Cache or retain              Selective                Extensive
     information                retrieval              useful results            preprocessing            preprocessing



Figure 4. Processing can move in either direction. Raw information still needs sufficient ingestion, security and
discoverability.

A demand-driven processing model
  Approach                              When it may be justified

  Preserve original sources             Maintain evidence, provenance, access controls and necessary metadata;
                                        comply with retention and deletion obligations.

  Process on retrieval                  A novel or infrequent need can tolerate on-demand computation. Use models
                                        or deterministic extractors matched to the task.

  Cache derived results                 Repeat retrievals justify reuse; retain provenance, freshness and invalidation
                                        rules.

  Preprocess selectively                Known repeated demand, latency, security, discoverability or regulatory
                                        requirements justify upfront investment.

  Re-evaluate and retire                Discard or recompute derived representations when use declines,
                                        requirements change or source data changes.


A useful comparison is the expected cost and value of preprocessing, storage and refresh versus
on-demand retrieval, including quality, latency and the likelihood of use. Keep canonical information
distinct from derived artifacts; avoid irreversible transformation and preserve necessary discoverability.
Some preprocessing, including protective controls, may be non-optional.




Valto Loikkanen | Conceptual whitepaper | November 2026                                                                   7
          LIQUID SOFTWARE / WHITEPAPER                                                    EXPANDED EDITION | NOV 2026




08 / DECISION PROTOCOL



Continuous capability economics
Liquid Software is not a one-time technology selection exercise. It is an operating discipline in which
agents and accountable humans repeatedly evaluate the realization of capabilities. The appropriate
implementation may be fully deterministic, fully agentic or hybrid.

  Decision step                          Practical question

  1. Specify the capability              What outcome, constraints and interaction contracts must remain true?

  2. Check existing resources            Can an existing service, module, skill or model fulfill this need?

  3. Execute and observe                 Where safe, meet the need now; record usage, costs, exceptions, quality
                                         and time to value.

  4. Compare alternatives                What is the expected net value over time, including risk, transition costs,
                                         reuse, rigidity and alternative uses of resources?

  5. Materialize selectively             What part merits deterministic realization? Can interfaces preserve
                                         off-ramps and fallback?

  6. Govern and revisit                  What permissions, tests, audit records, monitoring and review triggers are
                                         required?

  7. Evolve or dissolve                  Does this implementation still justify its existence? Preserve necessary
                                         information and controls while replacing or retiring it.


Informed selection and maturity bias
A decision-maker should understand and ideally have experienced the full available spectrum before
recommending an operating model. A lower-level implementation may be the informed optimum;
selecting it because more flexible alternatives were invisible is a different matter. Unknown alternatives
may remain even at the highest recognized maturity level.

This connects Liquid Software to the companion whitepaper, AI Maturity, Maturity Bias and Informed
Selection. The measure of maturity is not the absence of software, but the ability to continuously
optimize its existence and the realization of capabilities while respecting human-defined authority.


   Instead of making every tool intelligent, give intelligence access to
   every appropriate tool. Specialize only where the economics and
   requirements justify it.




Valto Loikkanen | Conceptual whitepaper | November 2026                                                                8
          LIQUID SOFTWARE / WHITEPAPER                                             EXPANDED EDITION | NOV 2026

# Beyond the Constraints of Software — Research Draft 00
URL: https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/drafts/00-beyond-the-constraints-of-software/
Status: research-draft
Conceptual source: Valto Loikkanen

# Beyond the Constraints of Software

*The transition toward an information-centric, intelligence-native world*


**Conceptual source and direction: Valto Loikkanen.** Research and drafting: Codex (OpenAI), at his request. Research draft 1.0 · 26 November 2026.

## Abstract

Software has enabled extraordinary progress while imposing a less visible constraint: people often must express their information, activities and ambitions in forms that existing applications can accommodate. Valto Loikkanen proposes reversing this relationship. Preserve information and its ownership over time; establish meaningful human decisions and boundaries; let intelligence interpret needs; and create, retain or retire software according to the value it provides. This paper introduces that synthesis and maps fifteen complementary papers. It argues for a change in architectural priorities, rather than a prediction that software, structure or institutions will disappear. Its contribution is a connected model of information continuity, adaptive interaction, evolving implementation and delegated human authority. [S01]

## 1. The constraint that became an organizing principle

Consider a small organization that wants to understand why a project changed direction. Its evidence may include an original conversation, a spreadsheet, an approval, a customer message and a later correction. One application preserves the spreadsheet, another the conversation, and another the approval. The question belongs to the organization, but answering it requires navigating the divisions imposed by its tools.

The same mismatch appears at several levels. A database records anticipated fields; a document selects a narrative; a dashboard selects indicators; an API exposes chosen operations; and an application admits a defined workflow. Each selection is useful. Trouble arises when the selection becomes the only surviving information or the only permitted way to use it.

The historical problem is therefore an inversion of priorities. Temporary choices about representation and execution become permanent constraints on information and human activity. Software is one contributor to this inversion, alongside institutions, incentives, physical limits and imperfect knowledge. Calling it a structural bottleneck identifies a mechanism to investigate, rather than a complete explanation of economic history. [S19]

## 2. The proposed reversal

Loikkanen's synthesis has four enduring concerns: whose interests are served, what information survives, what capabilities mean, and which decisions have already been made. Around these, interfaces and implementations can change at different speeds. [S01]

An **information-centric system** preserves attributable information independently of a particular presentation or application. An **intelligence-native system** can interpret emerging needs and select suitable ways to fulfill them. **Liquid Software** describes the changing implementations that support those needs. **Degrees of Decision Freedom** describe the space in which humans and their delegated actors may adapt without repeating decisions already settled at a higher level.

These concepts reinforce one another. A generated interface is useful when it can reach reliable information. A changing backend is sustainable when the capability retains meaning. An autonomous optimizer is acceptable when its authority is bounded. Ownership is practical when information and relationships survive the replacement of the current tool.

The separately supplied AI-assisted umbrella synthesis names four inversions across storage, retrieval, interfaces and software. Evidence is retained before anticipated questions narrow it; retrieval responds to new needs; interaction follows context; and implementations follow useful capability. This provides a parallel reading path through the same discussion, with its conceptual-source attribution and research limits preserved. [S30, pp. 2–4, 12]

## 3. Languages and formats are ways of interacting

The conversation's later clarification is essential: begin by treating interaction mechanisms as languages and formats through which a participant expresses a need or receives information. Natural language, a structured query, a diagram and a machine message can all play this role. The architectural question is what the interaction means, who it serves and how it can be fulfilled. [S01, S26]

Technical specifications remain useful for interoperability, but they need not dictate the full conceptual model. A schema may be generated from shared terminology, inferred under documented conventions, or negotiated for a particular exchange. Its existence does not imply a permanently designed application or database. Conversely, recognizable syntax alone does not establish shared meaning: two participants can use the same field name for different concepts.

The receiving system must resolve both meaning and authority. The requester contributes its need and desired representation; the receiver contributes available information, supported capabilities and disclosure boundaries. Intelligence can help reconcile these within previously established guidance. When it cannot, the system should expose the unresolved question rather than fabricate agreement.

## 4. A model with different rates of change

| Concern | What should persist | What may adapt |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Principals | Identity, relationships and delegated authority | Representatives and service providers |
| Information | Originals, provenance and accepted revisions | Indexes, interpretations and projections |
| Capabilities | Purpose, boundaries and meaningful outcomes | Agentic, hybrid and software realizations |
| Interaction | Agreed meaning and applicable commitments | Languages, formats and contextual presentation |
| Governance | Human decisions and external obligations | Operational choices within delegated freedom |

Persistence is not immutability. A corrected decision or revised capability must be able to change deliberately, with its history preserved. Fluidity is likewise not continuous mutation: a stable implementation may remain the best choice for years.

PIOS and EIOS are relevant public framework proposals for the personal and entity information foundations. CRD supplies capability documentation; PAIX explores contact and communication across independent participants. They contextualize the synthesis without being mandatory components of every adoption. Their publications are framework evidence, not independent proof of the complete vision. [S07–S10]

## 5. The collection and its independent questions

Papers 01–03 examine the software bottleneck, intelligence as a starting capability, and human decision freedom. Papers 04–07 define Liquid Software, adaptive interfaces, preservation for unknown future value, and adaptive retrieval. Papers 08–12 develop the optimizer, emerging interfaces, capability documentation, principals and the software lifecycle. Papers 13–15 examine internet economics, the transition to information-centric computing, and a composable reference architecture.

Paper 00 supplies the intellectual entry point. Paper 14 examines how to change existing systems. Paper 15 describes how the components can interact. Keeping these purposes distinct allows a reader to use one paper without adopting the entire collection.

## 6. What changes economically and socially

If adaptation becomes inexpensive and reliable, previously uneconomic needs may become serviceable. A person could obtain a specialized tool without waiting for a mass-market product; an organization could reshape a workflow around its own information; and a supplier could provide a capability through several interaction formats.

These possibilities do not guarantee decentralization. Compute, distribution, trusted data and liability could become more concentrated even as interface generation becomes easier. The relevant question is whether users gain effective choice: can they change a provider while preserving their information, commitments and working capability?

Human decision speed may become a limiting factor in some workflows. The remedy proposed here is to make a prior decision usable across many later actions. This requires understandable delegation and enforceable boundaries, alongside opportunities for human revision. It is a governance hypothesis, not a reason to remove human involvement wherever software can act.

## 7. A transition that can be tested

A useful first experiment starts with one existing information need. Preserve its sources, define the capability, establish a bounded interaction and compare three ways of serving it: existing software, direct intelligent execution and a combination. Measure total effort, quality, latency, recovery and the ability to change the implementation without changing the meaning.

Then observe actual demand. If repetition justifies a specialized implementation, build it and test whether it preserves permissions, provenance and behavior. If demand declines, withdraw the implementation while retaining the promised capability or explicitly renegotiating its availability.

The synthesis would be weakened if adaptation consistently costs more than it saves, shared semantics fail across participants, human delegation becomes opaque, or source preservation makes systems unusable. These are central research questions, not peripheral implementation details.

## 8. Intellectual lineage and contribution

The collection acknowledges existing work on malleable software, local-first ownership, dynamic computational media, data independence and end-to-end correctness. It extends the conversation's account by connecting these concerns to capability continuity, evolving retrieval and operational delegation. [S04–S06, S18, S20, S21]

Valto Loikkanen is the source of the conceptual synthesis developed here. This attribution does not claim that every component or the term Liquid Software originated with him; JFrog's earlier use of that term concerns continuous software delivery. The present research draft offers an explicit, testable interpretation of his connected argument. [S03]

# The Software Bottleneck — Research Draft 01
URL: https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/drafts/01-the-software-bottleneck/
Status: research-draft
Conceptual source: Valto Loikkanen

# The Software Bottleneck

*How implementation rigidity shapes the opportunities people can pursue*


**Conceptual source and direction: Valto Loikkanen.** Research and drafting: Codex (OpenAI), at his request. Research draft 1.0 · 26 November 2026.

## Abstract

Software can constrain activity when adapting it costs more than the value of a particular need. Valto Loikkanen identifies this rigidity as a structural bottleneck and argues that intelligence may make adaptation responsive to actual demand. This paper defines the bottleneck, identifies its economic mechanism and distinguishes coding speed from useful flexibility. It proposes measurements that include lost opportunities, workarounds, maintenance and human attention. The argument is conditional: reducing implementation friction can move constraints elsewhere without eliminating them. [S01]

## 1. Needs that never become features

A user wants a report that combines several sources for a decision this afternoon. The desired report is understandable, but no application provides it. A developer could build the feature, yet specification, integration and maintenance make the request too expensive. The user accepts an incomplete view, creates a manual workaround or abandons the question.

This is an illustrative case, not an empirical observation from a named organization. It exposes a demand that ordinary software metrics may miss. A feature backlog records some requests; it rarely records all questions people stopped asking because they expected the answer to be impractical.

Define the **software bottleneck** as the constraint arising when the availability, cost or adaptability of implementations limits an otherwise meaningful and authorized activity. It can appear in development queues, rigid information models, integration gaps and the cognitive effort of navigating tools.

## 2. The economic mechanism

An adaptation is pursued when its expected benefit exceeds development, coordination, operation and maintenance costs. Centralized products therefore prioritize needs shared by many users. Specialized requests may remain below the commercial threshold even when they are valuable to a particular person or group.

The result is not simply missing features. Users reshape their processes around the product: they enter data in the offered categories, perform extra steps, or omit useful distinctions. The tool influences which activities seem possible and which information survives. Loikkanen's broader thesis is that this influence can extend to organizational and market arrangements. That extension requires evidence beyond a coding demonstration. [S01]

Ink & Switch's malleable-software research offers related accounts of users adapting their workflows to inflexible tools. Its emphasis is user agency and modification at the point of use. The present paper frames the resulting adaptation gap as a constraint on pursuing opportunities. [S04]

## 3. Coding speed is one part of flexibility

Generating a working script more quickly can reduce a particular cost. It does not resolve ambiguous requirements, inaccessible information, integration authority, security obligations or long-term support. Brooks's distinction between difficulties intrinsic to a system's conceptual design and difficulties of representing it remains a useful counterweight to sweeping automation claims. [S19]

Useful flexibility has at least four dimensions:

- **Expression:** can someone communicate the actual need without learning the internal model of an application?
- **Fulfillment:** can the system assemble an appropriate capability from available information and tools?
- **Adaptation:** can the implementation change while preserving meaningful behavior and accepted work?
- **Continuity:** can the user retain information and commitments when a tool or provider changes?

A system may improve one dimension while worsening another. A custom interface might be easy to generate but impossible to maintain; a broad agent might understand requests but lack reliable access to the necessary records.

## 4. Where intelligence may change the threshold

Intelligence can help interpret an unfamiliar request, find relevant information, compose existing tools and produce a temporary interface. Repetition can then justify a specialized implementation. This sequence changes the threshold for serving an emerging need: usefulness can be established before committing to a permanent feature.

The claim is not that every need should begin with an agent. A proven deterministic capability may already be cheaper and more dependable. The proposed opportunity is to avoid requiring a new predefined implementation for every variation before any value can be delivered.

A recurring request for overdue commitments illustrates the mechanism. Initially, an agent might reconcile a few source documents. Later, consistent definitions and frequent demand may justify a structured projection and direct query. The capability becomes cheaper to serve while its original evidence remains available.

## 5. Measuring the bottleneck

| Measurement | Why it matters |
| --- | --- |
| Time from expressed need to useful result | Captures adaptation delay |
| Abandoned or deferred meaningful requests | Reveals demand omitted from shipped-feature metrics |
| Manual coordination and re-entry | Captures work displaced onto users |
| Total cost over a realistic period | Includes maintenance and validation |
| Decision quality and source coverage | Prevents speed from substituting for usefulness |
| Recovery and provider-switching effort | Measures continuity beyond first success |

A study should compare a stable baseline with a bounded adaptive alternative using similar tasks and participants. It should include negative results and failures. A demonstration that a tool can be generated is evidence of possibility; it does not establish sustained productivity or social impact.

Research on generative AI at work provides a useful reminder that benefits can vary by task and worker experience. The customer-support study by Brynjolfsson, Li and Raymond concerns a specific assistance setting, not liquid architectures across the economy. [S24]

## 6. Counterarguments

Standardization can be beneficial. It supports training, coordination, safety and comparability. A process that appears rigid may encode a deliberate agreement rather than a technical limitation. Before modifying it, distinguish unnecessary implementation constraints from legitimate shared rules.

Customization also has costs. People may struggle to learn continuously changing interfaces. Generated components can create dependency and support burdens. An adaptive system can become a more powerful monopoly if it owns the user's information, terminology and relationship history.

Finally, a bottleneck can move. Faster software production may expose unclear objectives, limited trust, fragmented authority or inadequate information. Solving implementation friction is valuable even when these remain, but it should not be reported as their solution.

## 7. Research and practical implications

Organizations can start by mapping where meaningful requests are blocked and why. A selected case should identify the information required, the actor authorized to act, the cost of the existing workaround and the smallest useful adaptation.

The central hypothesis is falsifiable: within an appropriately bounded domain, intelligence-assisted adaptation should make a wider range of useful needs serviceable at an acceptable total cost. The stronger societal thesis requires longitudinal evidence about agency, economic opportunity, concentration and outcomes.

The paper's contribution is to make the adaptation gap visible as an object of research. Liquid Software supplies one response to that gap; adaptive interfaces address expression; information preservation supports future fulfillment; and decision freedom addresses authority. None independently guarantees that the bottleneck disappears.


## Sources and attribution

**[S01]** Valto Loikkanen and ChatGPT. *Define liquid software — shared conversation*. Retrieved 26 November 2026. [Original source](https://chatgpt.com/share/6b077626-c894-83ed-aabf-d21a363c4313).

**[S04]** Geoffrey Litt, Josh Horowitz, Peter van Hardenberg and Todd Matthews. *Malleable Software: Restoring User Agency in a World of Locked-Down Apps*. June 2025. [Original source](https://www.inkandswitch.com/essay/malleable-software/).

**[S19]** Frederick P. Brooks, Jr.. *No Silver Bullet: Essence and Accidents of Software Engineering*. UNC technical report TR86-020, September 1986. [Original source](https://www.cs.unc.edu/techreports/86-020.pdf).

**[S24]** Erik Brynjolfsson, Danielle Li and Lindsey R. Raymond. *Generative AI at Work*. NBER Working Paper 31161, April 2023, revised November 2023; published QJE 140(2), 2025, pp. 889–942. [Original source](https://www.nber.org/papers/w31161).

Valto Loikkanen supplies the conceptual synthesis and directs this collection. Codex prepared the research and prose. Definitions and reference models are editorial developments of the cited discussion, not claimed verbatim statements or universal first inventions.
